description: eslint-plugin-react-hooks 7.1.1 react-hooks/rules-of-hooks: a hook call (`use`, `useX`, `Namespace.useX`) reported at its callee when it runs (its nearest function, ESLint's code path) in a component or hook (a function named `X…`/`useX`, or memo/forwardRef's callback) conditionally (an if/conditional/logical/switch/catch/default branch, or after an earlier return in the function); in a class method or field; in another named function; at the top level; in an anonymous callback inside a component or hook; in a loop; in an async component or hook; and `use` in try/catch. Code paths are approximated syntactically.

violation.message: React Hooks must be called in the exact same order in every component render, only in React function components or custom React Hook functions.
React Hooks must be called in the exact same order in every component render, only in React function components or custom React Hook functions.
React Hook may be executed more than once. Possibly because it is called in a loop.
React Hook cannot be called in an async function.
A function created with React Hook "useEffectEvent" can only be called from Effects and Effect Events in the same component.
React Hook "useEffectEvent" can only be called at the top level of your component. It cannot be passed down.
React Hook "use" cannot be called in a try/catch block.
